title: Rapid recovery and resilience strategy for Dedicated capacity shortfalls
creator: Ava Rodriguez
description:
Summary: During a sustained traffic spike on 2026-02-27 we observed a dedicated capacity shortfall affecting multiple customer pools. This ticket consolidates the rapid recovery steps taken, an operational after-action analysis, and a prioritized set of resilience changes (immediate mitigations and long-term hardening) to prevent recurrence. The focus is on autoscale policy tuning, fleet controls, headroom budgeting, and improved observability to detect scaling regressions faster.

Audience: on-call engineers, SREs, product owners for Dedicated, and the Reliability guild.

Scope: This doc covers the incident timeline, root cause hypotheses and evidence, short-term mitigations applied during the incident, design proposals for long-term fixes, runbook and alerting changes, and a prioritized action list with owners and estimated effort.
timeline:
2026-02-27 02:15 UTC: anomaly alert - sustained queue growth in three dedicated pools.
2026-02-27 02:20 UTC: automated autoscaler failed to add nodes due to a control-plane rate limit in the regional scheduler.
2026-02-27 02:28 UTC: on-call rotated traffic to lower-priority pools via emergency routing policy; latency recovered partially.
2026-02-27 02:55 UTC: incremental capacity provisioned using pre-warmed standby nodes; throughput returned to SLO by 03:10 UTC.
Post-incident: 2026-03-01: emergency follow-up to capture evidence and start remediation work.
root_cause: Primary contributing factor: a combination of (1) scheduler control-plane rate limits that prevented the autoscaler from converging within SLA, and (2) overly tight autoscaler hysteresis and cooldown settings that prevented rapid ramp-up once the control-plane resumed. Secondary factor: insufficient predictive headroom in pools that serve bursty traffic patterns (batching and prefix-cache miss storms). There was no single code bug causing crash; the failure mode was emergent from policy thresholds and operational limits under a correlated traffic spike.
steps_taken_during_incident:
- Enabled emergency routing policy to divert new requests to less-utilized pools and put non-critical customers into degraded mode.
- Triggered pre-warmed standby nodes in the region (manual override to bypass scheduler quiesce path).
- Increased autoscaler request retry backoff temporarily to overcome control-plane throttling.
- Rolled an emergency configuration that relaxed autoscale cooldown from 60s to 15s for impacted pools.
- Notified impacted customers and posted status updates to the SLA dashboard and support channels.
short_term_mitigations:
- Ship a hotfix: autoscaler will perform exponential retry with jitter and an adaptive retry cap when it receives 429/503 from the scheduler (target: next 48 hours).
- Deploy pre-warmed standby policy as default for pools flagged as 'burst-sensitive' with a small reserved headroom (2-4 nodes).
- Adjust default cooldown/hysteresis to be more aggressive for pools with median request size < 1s.
- Add synthetic traffic monitor to detect prefix-cache miss storms and trigger temporary cache warming on key models.
long_term_proposals:
- Scheduler resilience: move critical autoscaler control-plane calls to a higher-priority channel with per-tenant circuit breakers and quota reservations; explore optimistic local scaling that can temporarily add capacity without immediate control-plane confirmation. (Design RFC Q2)
- Predictive headroom: build workload classifier to assign burst sensitivity score to each pool; automatically set reserved capacity and pre-warm policies based on score.
- Autoscaler state machine revamp: introduce separate fast-path for emergency scale-ups with shorter stabilization windows and explicit rollback guards.
- Observability: add token-level and queue-length histograms to the console with retention for 30d, expose latent autoscaler error codes on per-fleet dashboard, and wire cross-region scheduling latency SLI alerts.
runbook_changes:
- New step: when queue-growth alert exceeds threshold and autoscaler errors contain >5% 429/503, immediately switch pool to emergency routing (documented command) and escalate to SRE lead.
- Add checklist for enabling standby pre-warms and rolling back emergency cooldown adjustments.
- Include explicit post-incident evidence collection steps: scheduler logs, autoscaler request traces, and traffic-shift timelines.
- Add owner for periodic (weekly) sampling of bursty pools to verify headroom settings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Hotfix deployed to all regions and verified in canary within 48 hours.
- Four pilot burst-sensitive pools configured with pre-warm policy; no capacity shortfall under synthetic spike test (3x expected peak) in staging.
- New autoscaler metrics and dashboard tiles live in Console and alert rules validated.
- RFC for scheduler resilience merged and prioritized into Q2 roadmap.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-94601: implement exponential retry with jitter for autoscaler control-plane calls - owner: S. Kline - 3 pts
ENG-94605: implement pool burst classifier and pre-warm config tooling - owner: M. Chen - 8 pts
ENG-94612: dashboard panels for autoscaler error rates and scheduler latency - owner: R. Patel - 2 pts
ENG-94620: RFC for optimistic local scale-up and control-plane reservation - owner: A. Rodriguez - 5 pts
post_incident_notes:
Lessons learned: configuration surface area (cooldown/hysteresis) is a first-class reliability parameter and must be tied to workload characteristics rather than a global default. Control-plane throttling is a real ops boundary that requires both smarter client-side retries and explicit quota/priority lanes. Communication cadence with customer ops worked well; update templates for faster customer-facing summaries.

Open risks: optimistic local scaling increases risk of transient over-provisioning and billing anomalies; needs quota and rollback safeguards. The scheduler work is non-trivial and will require cross-team alignment with Orchestration and Billing to avoid resource accounting regressions.
notes: Current owner is Samuel Kline (assignee). Weekly sync scheduled starting 2026-03-11 to track follow-up progress. Recommend a tabletop exercise in Q2 to validate new runbook steps and pre-warm behaviors.
